growth_signal.value: Revenue grew about fivefold in a year and customers nearly tripled; its site says 150,000+ organisations use it

raised.value: $94.7M in total, including a $60M Series B led by DST Global at a $1B valuation

entry.idea: One security tool that checks everything a software team writes and runs, and fixes most problems itself, so developers stop drowning in false alarms.
entry.lesson: Sell to the person who feels the pain daily, make the first taste free, and let usage pull the enterprise contract behind it.
entry.name: Aikido Security

growth.reason: Fivefold revenue growth in a year and Europe's fastest cybersecurity unicorn, three years after founding.

market.reason: Every company that writes software needs this, and AI-written code is multiplying the need.

tech.reason: Well-built and broad, but security scanning is a crowded field where large rivals can catch up.

sources.title: Belgian cybersecurity startup Aikido hits unicorn status (Reuters via Yahoo)
Aikido Security raises $60M Series B at $1B valuation (press release)
Aikido raises $60M at a $1B valuation (company blog)

entry.twist: It sells to the developers rather than the security department, is free to start, and claims 99% fewer false alarms than the fragmented tools it replaces.
entry.who_pays: Software companies pay per team once they outgrow the free tier; customers include Revolut, SoundCloud and Niantic.
entry.why_now: AI now writes a large share of code, and companies need guardrails that work at that speed without a security team reviewing every line.
